flags.name: Herb Chives [Market]
flags.issue: THE MARKET BUNCH IS COSTED AT THE SINGLE-BUNCH PRICE — 4.1x too cheap, in the flattering direction, and live in the picker today. The feed emits $2.42 per bunch. $2.42 is unambiguously HCBCH, the SINGLE bunch, from FFT invoice INB00114866 (2026-08-12, billed to Harry Gatos); the MARKET bunch is HCMB and is chef-confirmed at $0.0792/g = $9.90 a bunch (data/costs.csv carries HCMB at that rate from INB00099534 onward and labels it 'chef-confirmed'). The cause is in data/product_map.csv: TWO FFT codes are bridged onto the ONE Lightspeed id 22995343 — 'Fresh Fruit Team,HCBCH,22995343,Herb Chives [Market],,,,,recipe-bridge' with no venue, alongside the correct 'Fresh Fruit Team,HCMB,22995343,Herb Chives [Market],stowaway,zak-confirmed 2026-08-18'. HCBCH is ALSO bridged to 22493903 ('chives'), which is where it belongs. This is the exact pair triage item 13 recorded: the two survived a name collapse only while the parser truncated one of them, and the tiebreak prefers the cheaper row.
flags.suggested_fix: Remove the HCBCH -> 22995343 recipe-bridge row from data/product_map.csv, leaving HCMB -> 22995343 (market bunch, $9.90) and HCBCH -> 22493903 (single bunch, $2.42). NOT EDITED HERE: product_map is the bridge ledger, this moves money between two live price series, and the 2026-08-21 note already in data/cogs_list.csv against this id says a previous attempt to fix it by relabelling the unit was tried and REVERTED. That note also states the durable fix is a BUNCH WEIGHT for the [Market] bunch rather than a unit relabel — a chef confirming grams per market bunch would settle both. Also note this bridge violates the 2026-08-20 hard constraint against two bridges on one anchor when the invoices are cross-venue: HCBCH's invoices bill to Harry Gatos, HCMB's to Stowaway.

mentions.name: Garlic Black
mentions.note: PACK NOT CONFIRMED AND DELIBERATELY NOT GUESSED. needs_pack_review is TRUE, so it is already going to the chef. Invoice INB00116225 (2026-08-21) was opened and states raw_uom 'Pack' and nothing more — qty 2 Pack, $15.12 each, $30.24. The supplier's own code reads GB-220G-PK, which strongly implies a 220 g pack ($68.73/kg, which is the right order for black garlic), but a pack size inferred from a code string is not a stated fact and this pipeline has been burned by exactly that kind of plausible reading. Confirm on the FFT catalogue or with the chef before it goes in pack_overrides.

mentions.name: BAMBOO SKEWERS 100PC 20CM 8INCH Pak Imports
mentions.note: needs_pack_review TRUE, so already visible to the chef. The pack IS stated — 100PC, in the product's own name — it just is not a unit the parser knows, so pack_qty came back null. At $2.20 a pack that is $0.022 a skewer. A kitchen consumable rather than food, but triage item 11 established that consumables and packaging belong in the picker by design (Marilyna's pizza boxes are costed per each), so no exclusion is proposed.

mentions.name: Herb Basil
mentions.note: Per BUNCH at $4.95 with needs_pack_review FALSE, i.e. no grams-per-bunch, on a herb every recipe measures by mass. This is the KNOWN per-bunch class named in the 2026-08-20 coverage ruling (Parsley, Lime, Lemon, Brown Onions) and it needs a chef to confirm the bunch weight — not re-derived here. Checked for the chives trap and it is NOT present: FFT has no market-bunch basil code, and the only other live basil is select-fresh:HBAS at $4.60/bunch, a consistent second reading rather than a conflicting one. Neither is bridged onto a shared Lightspeed anchor.

mentions.name: Turkish Bread [ea]
mentions.note: LOOKED WRONG AND IS NOT — checked rather than flagged. A name saying '[ea]' carrying a unit of 'g' at $0.008167 is the shape that usually means a per-each price got a per-gram unit. It resolves: data/product_map.csv bridges it to Urbun Bakery TFB120, 'Turkish/Focaccia Bread (120g)' at $0.98 a loaf (OMI298891, 2026-08-15), and 0.98 / 120 = 0.008167 exactly. costs.csv labels the row 'chef-confirmed (via urbun-bakery:TFB120)'. Correct, and the bridge is doing what it is for.
